name: Orb models (Orbital Materials)
origin_detail: Orbital Materials (now Orbital Industries), a VC-backed startup whose commercial products (CurieOS platform, licensed discovery) are proprietary (see E/orbital-materials.json).

licences.weights: Apache-2.0 ('Orb models are licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0')
licences.data: trained on public datasets (OMol25 confirmed for OrbMol); no own training data release found

openness_notes: Code and weights Apache-2.0 since Orb-v1 (Sep 2024). OrbMol was 'Trained on the Open Molecules 2025 (OMol25) dataset' and OrbMol-v2 on OMol25 + OPoly26. Training data for v1-v3 are not named on the fetched page (the checkpoint name orb-v3-conservative-inf-omat suggests OMat24). Models trained on Meta's CC BY 4.0 datasets carry Apache-2.0, unlike Meta's own custom-licensed UMA or Cambridge's ASL MACE-OMAT-0. Group I scoring: 0 = no weights; 1 = weights only under non-commercial or gated custom terms; 2 = open code/weights with the flagship model, weights or training data closed (open core); 3 = code and weights under OSI-type or CC BY licences; 4 = 3 plus openly downloadable training data, or outputs published as an open database stewarded by a public institution. Score 3 (permissive code and weights; the company's platform is proprietary).
robustness: Apache-2.0 weights; trained on public data, so retraining is possible in principle.
physical_science_relevance: Fast universal MLIPs for materials and molecular simulation; used commercially for cooling and carbon-capture materials (company).

training_data.name: v1-v3 training data
training_data.note: Not named on fetched page; likely MPtrj/Alexandria/OMat24.

openness_effect_assessment: A startup used Apache-2.0 models trained on public data as visibility and recruiting assets, while selling proprietary discovery services. The permissive weights make Orb the commercially usable option on OMat24/OMol25 data.
key_takeaway: Startups in materials AI tend to open the model and close the application, the reverse of the protein startups (Chai, Boltz) that open older models and close the newest.
